issues.title: Bug: new game starts with the hero wearing the Obsidian Sovereign chest
issues.body:
Owner report (2026-10-28), with a Play screenshot at WAVE 0, gold 0: the hero stands in the courtyard wearing the dark Obsidian Sovereign chest (arrow emblem) over the silver hero armour, nothing bought.

> why does game start with me wearing this?

**Expected:** a new game starts in the plain silver armour. The Obsidian chest only shows after buying it at Vesna and equipping it.

**Master's finding (16:25):** the swap itself is correct: `ObsidianChest` on the hero uses `MI_ObsidianSovereign_Chest_Hero` (ArmorMode -1, show only when worn) and `MPC_SkillTree Armor.R` is 0 in the editor. What turns it on at runtime is the **armoury save slot** `CastleSaveArmory.sav`: the HUD loads it on start and writes Armor.R = ObsV worn every frame, so a chest bought and equipped in an earlier session is still worn at wave 0. **Owner decision needed:** does the armoury carry over between games (meta-progression), or does Begin the Siege start fresh and only Continue load it?

**Original suspects**
1. `MPC_SkillTree Armor.R` is still at the Obsidian value in the editor: material parameter collections keep the last value set, so the swap survives into the next Play. Fix: reset it to 0 on BeginPlay of a new game (before the armoury load), and in the asset default. (`Tools\master\mpc_armor_check.py` reads/resets it.)
2. The armoury save slot (CastleSaveArmory) still has the chest marked owned/worn from a test: a New Game must ignore or clear it; only Continue loads it.

issues.title: Bug: several zombies attacking at once launch the hero very high into the air (fixed)
issues.body:
Owner report (2026-10-29): when several spawned zombies attack the hero at once they push him into the air and keep pushing, and he flies very high.

**Cause** (BP_Zombie attack, ApplyDamage → LaunchCharacter(player)): knockback velocity = Normalize(hero − zombie) × 1100 + (0,0,550), Z override on. The direction was 3D, so once the hero was a little above a zombie every hit pointed upward (up to +1650 cm/s) and the next hit relaunched him from even higher.

**Fix** (hossam gmail (Claude), saved): new velocity block wired into the same LaunchCharacter: flat direction (Z removed) × 800, plus Z = +180 hop only if the hero is less than 60 cm above the zombie, otherwise −150 (pulls him back down). Hits can no longer stack upward. Old math nodes left unconnected. Backup: Tools/ClaudeCmd/backup_1029/BP_Zombie_pre_knock.uasset.

Owner to confirm in Play with a crowd of zombies.

issues.title: Scene is too dark: lift shadows and exposure without losing the bleak mood
issues.body:
Owner comment (2026-10-28): a friend said the scene is very dark; in shade it is, and even in a sunny area it's still a bit dark. Owner agrees, but the depressive, bleak mood must stay.

**Approach (brighten what the eye reads, keep the mood):** the mood comes from low saturation, the grey-olive tint, overcast sky, fog and contrast between light and shade; darkness itself isn't needed. So lift the darkest values and the exposure floor, and leave colour, fog and sky as they are.
1. **Auto-exposure floor:** raise Min EV100 (and/or exposure compensation +0.3-0.5) in the master post-process volume, so shaded areas don't sink to near-black; keep Max EV so the sunny areas don't blow out.
2. **Local Exposure (UE 5.1+):** turn on post-process Local Exposure (highlight contrast ~0.8, shadow contrast ~0.6-0.7) to open up shadows while keeping the bright areas the same.
3. **Fill light, not sun:** sky light intensity up a little (2.0 -> ~2.4) and lower its occlusion so courtyard shade and the field get more ambient light; don't make the sun stronger.
4. **Grade:** shadows gain/offset lifted slightly (milky, desaturated blacks instead of crushed black); keep saturation, the 20% green sky tint, the grey overcast and the wave grade exactly as now.
5. **Player option:** a Brightness/Gamma slider in Settings (default = new look), since monitors differ.
6. Check spots: courtyard in the shade of the walls, gate tunnel, field road at dusk, wave fights, the portal area.

issues.title: Bug: holding the crossbow, Space makes the hero fly into the sky
issues.body:
﻿Owner: **while idle holding the crossbow, pressing Space makes the hero fly up into the sky** instead of jumping.

**What the exports show (checkking, from BP_Crossbow.t3d / BP_ThirdPersonCharacter.t3d)**
- The hero has a single, normal jump binding (`IA_Jump` Started -> `Jump`, Completed -> `StopJumping`), so the jump itself isn't doubled.
- While the crossbow is equipped (`IMC_Crossbow` mapped), `BP_Crossbow` Tick **keeps the aim montage `AM_Xbow_Aim` playing at all times** and scrubs it every frame with `Montage_SetPosition`; since #19 (#26) its play rate is **0** (held pose).
- **Prime suspect:** that montage (or its sequence `AS_Xbow_AimSweep`) has **root motion enabled**. A root-motion montage drives the character's velocity; held at rate 0 it feeds zero root motion while the jump's upward velocity is never pulled down by gravity, so the hero keeps rising. If this started after the #26 paste, that confirms it.

**Fix options (pick one)**
1. Open `AS_Xbow_AimSweep` and turn **Enable Root Motion off** (it's an upper-body aim pose, it shouldn't move the capsule). Safest.
2. Or in `BP_Crossbow` Tick, skip `Montage_Play` / `Montage_SetPosition` when `CharacterMovement.IsFalling` and stop the aim montage on jump.
3. Or play the aim pose on an upper-body **slot** with root motion mode "Ignore Root Motion" in the hero AnimBP.

**Checks**
1. Equip the crossbow, stand idle, press Space: a normal jump, landing normally.
2. Jump while aiming (RMB) and while walking: normal jumps.

issues.title: Water and fire sounds far too loud up close
issues.body:
﻿Owner: the **water and fire sounds are very loud** when standing **in front of or beside** them (fountain / waterfall / river, torches / campfires / braziers).

**Likely causes to check**
- The ambient cues have **no attenuation** or a very small **inner radius**, so they play at full volume close up (or are 2D and not spatialised at all).
- **Stacking:** many torches and fires each play their own loop, so standing between several adds them up. Needs a **concurrency** limit (e.g. max 3 fire loops, quietest stopped).
- Volume multipliers left above 1 from the audio pass.

**Fix**
- One shared **Sound Attenuation** asset per family (`SA_Fire`, `SA_Water`): inner radius about 1-2 m, a natural log falloff to about 15-25 m (water) / 8-12 m (torches), spatialisation on, and a gentle low-pass with distance.
- A **Sound Concurrency** per family (fire: max 3-4, water: max 2) with "stop quietest".
- Base volume so standing right next to a torch is comfortable and the music and combat stay clearly on top.

**Checks**
1. Stand next to a torch, then the fountain, then the waterfall: clearly audible but not overpowering, no clipping.
2. Walk away: fades out smoothly; no sudden cut.
3. Stand between several torches: no loudness pile-up.
